description: Six crossings from an A2A task into an MCP tool invocation, declared before the exact-crossing binding is implemented. Each case is run in two lanes and the predicted outcome in each lane is recorded here, in advance.

lanes.native: A2A caller and MCP server composed directly. Each side authenticates by its own rules. No crossing receipt.
lanes.bound: The identical composition with a Border exact-crossing binding carried as an A2A extension reference, rechecked by Gate before the MCP action runs.

action.why: Harmless and side-effect free. The experiment is about whether authority survived a handoff, not about causing an effect.

cases.role: Positive control. If the valid path does not succeed in BOTH lanes the experiment is void, because every later refusal would be consistent with a broken lane rather than with a seam defect.

cases.mutation: the A2A task is presented by a different caller identity than the one the authority was issued to
cases.role: A2A leaves authorization models largely implementation-defined. Whether a native composition notices the substitution is exactly what is being measured, so it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

cases.mutation: taskId or contextId replaced with another live task's identifier
cases.role: Tests whether the authority is bound to the specific task or merely to a well-formed one.

cases.mutation: the MCP tool name or its arguments differ from what the authority named
cases.role: The crossing is where an authority for action X can become an invocation of action Y without either side seeing an anomaly.

cases.mutation: a previously valid crossing authorization is presented a second time
cases.role: Freshness across the handoff, as distinct from freshness within either protocol.

cases.mutation: the authority is expired or revoked at the moment of the MCP invocation
cases.role: Revocation must be evaluated at the crossing, not only at issuance.

interest_condition: The experiment is interesting only if valid_crossing succeeds in BOTH lanes AND at least one of the five mutations passes ordinary component checks in the native lane while being rejected in the bound lane.
refutation: If every mutation is already caught in the native lane, there is no seam gap to own and A2A-MCP-CROSSING-001 reports that result. That outcome is publishable and must be published rather than discarded.
not_claimed: This file does not assert that an exploitable A2A or MCP defect exists. The five 'unknown' predictions are unknown on purpose. Any claim of a seam gap must be earned by running this.
